a dissected loess upland seen from directly above, deep narrow ravines branching in a tree pattern through pale yellow-buff silt, steep vertical walls, rounded knolls and flat ridges of dry ochre earth between them, hard shadow down one side of every ravine, no terraces, no steps, no green, no plants, no rock, no sand; transition: the meadow grass thinning onto dry buff silt, the first shallow gullies opening in the bare earth
items.note: the first loess asked for stepped terraces and came back a flat orange fill with no relief at all: the terraced staircase of every modern photograph of the plateau is a later engineering campaign, and asking for it first put the gullies second and got neither. Loess cleaves vertically, so the landform is dissection rather than steps -- gullies, and the flat-topped tableland, ridge, and knoll left between them. The second named those and forbade the terraces and still came back flat: standard mode draws a texture, and a dendritic gully network is geometry. Four more were run side by side and compared as autotiled patches over grass (`var/scratch/loess-cand.mts`): harder shading gave a fainter hatch on the same flat ground, `badlands` gave a regular diagonal corduroy that reads as weaving, `large simple landforms` gave a blank cream shelf, and pro mode with `raggedness` 0.55 drew the branching tree outright. The lesson is which knob answers: shading and wording move the texture, and only pro's shape controls move the landform

items.note: the first steppe forbade bare earth and brown soil twice and the generator supplied both anyway, in rows of discrete cruciform plants with bright lime shoots over mid-brown ground: a planted row crop, not grassland. Naming a colour the ground is not gets a colour the ground is not; the second describes the sward positively -- gold, straw, and olive, laid over in wind-combed streaks, grass touching grass with no gaps -- and drops the adjust that was pushing what came back further toward yellow

items.prompt: high rolling downland seen from directly above, each hill a broad dome of fresh light green turf, the crown a bright yellow-green catching the sun and only the lower side carrying a soft grey-green shadow, the hollows between them a light sage green, fine grass texture over the whole surface, plainly greener and lighter than the meadow around it, no dark green, no deep green, no black, no white, no cream, no ivory, no grey stone, no rock, no bare earth, no pink, no mauve, no violet; transition: the meadow rising gently onto the first shoulder, the grass lightening as it climbs, nothing but grass
items.note: the third sheet had the shape but read as low ground: dark green shadow per dome, deeper green in the hollows, and an adjust that dropped both saturation and value. High ground catches light. The fourth put the whole crown in pale green-grey and went past green into cream, so the domes read as pebbles on a paper cut-out. The fifth keeps the crown bright and the shadow a narrow band on the lower side alone and forbids both ends, and came back an acid lime: that last step is a palette, not a shape, so the adjust turns it toward green and takes half its saturation out rather than spending a sixth generation. The adjust was retuned 2026-08-25 after `splitFinish` stopped handing the downland's own turf to the meadow: half the sheet had been repainted in grass's lightest shade, so the adjust was only ever finishing the crown, and applied to the whole body it left crown and turf twenty luminance apart in mint. It now keeps four fifths of the generation's saturation and drops an eighth of its value, which puts the shadow under the meadow, the turf a clear grade over it, and the crown over that
